Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your secret
communication of May 8 transmitting a document
forwarded to you by the Criminal Intelligence
Department of the Straits Settlements Government.

Considerable time has been given to this
investigation which included a watch on the address
given in the document, discreet visits to the shop
itself and an arrangement with the Chinese Postal
Censors to intercept all mail matter addressed to
Mr. Yik Sia Kong ( ) or the Chu Young Book
Store ( ). During a period of four
weeks no communication so addressed passed through
the Post Office and efforts in other directions
brought to light nothing beyond the fact that the
premises could without difficulty be used as a
communication office.

On June 5, 1930, however, the Shanghai
Special District Court, at the instance of the local
Chinese authorities, issued a warrant for the arrest
of all persons found in the premises of this establishment

(C.I.D.) Office Notes                                      June 14, 1930.

Special Branch No. 1

Chiu Young Book Store, No. 176 Chengtu Road

With reference to H.B.M. Consul-General's commu-
nication of May 8 transmitting translation of a letter addressed
to the Provisional Committee of the South Seas Communist
Party, Singapore, from "Central" Shanghai, which was seen
by the Straits Settlements Government in transit I beg to
report that investigations into the contents of the letter
show that the shop given therein as Mr. Yih Siu-kong (葉光),
Chiu Young Book Store, No.176 Chengtu Road, was engaged in
the sale of books of a pro-communist nature. A raid carried
out by the Municipal Police on a Special District Court
warrant on June 5, 1930, resulted in the arrest of four
persons named respectively, Wang Zoong-ling (王仲鏻 ), Yang
Ying-sien (楊印光 ), Woo Shou-fan (胡孝藩 ) and Tsuan
Tseng-hua (詹振華 ), and the seizure of a quantity of
pamphlets and more than 1,000 copies of four different kinds
of books bearing the following titles :-

1. Materialistic philosophy.
2. Materialism and religion.
3. Oulinoff, the Materialist.
4. Soviet farmers and women.

The prisoners appeared before the 2nd Branch,
Kiangsu High Court on June 6, when they were remanded sine
die. A copy of translation of Court Proceedings together
with statements of each prisoner is attached.

Despite a careful search of the shop, nothing was
discovered to show that this address was used as a communi-
cating place for the delegates to the International Labour
Conference to be held in Shanghai.

My name is He Sheu-fan, native of Hwaian Hsien, Anhui, age
28. I was born in Anhui and my father named He Ling-ken who
was a farmer died fifteen years ago. I have a brother, named
He Sieu-chi. At 12 years of age I studied with my brother
at home. Two years later I studied at one of my relatives.
Three years later I studied in a private school belonging to
a fellow countryman named Tong for two years. At 19 years
of age I began to study in a private school belonging to a
fellow countryman named Teng where I remained for two years.
Later I studied about one year at Wuhu and owing to poor
financial conditions at home I discontinued my studies and
one year later I became a teacher in a certain Meng's private
school at a salary of $50 per annum. I taught for about
two years and returned home as that school was closed. I
remained at home till last autumn when I was engaged by the
5th Primary School of the 3rd District of Sheu Hsien in
Anhui as a teacher at a salary of $170 per annum.
About 18th of May this year I accompanied my nephew and
brother-in-law to Shanghai for the purpose of seeking
apprenticeship for them. On arriving in Shanghai we took
up residence with a fellow countryman named Ho Shih-you in
the Foo Ming Flour Mill. My nephew secured an apprenticeship
in the Yah Ta Factory through the efforts of Ho Shih-you,
but my brother-in-law has not succeeded yet. That is why
I have not returned home. On the afternoon of the 5th inst.
I went to the Chu Yang Book Store to call on a friend named
Wang Hiao-mei. On arriving at the book store I met Mr. Wang

THE NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JUNE 17, 1930

TRIAL IN COURT
OF MIXEN

Important Point Raised in Connection with Alleged
Communists

SEQUEL TO A RAID BY
POLICE

An interesting point relating to the jurisdiction of this Court was raised this morning in the case of Wong Zoong-ling, Yang Ying-sien, Woo Zur-van and Tseu Tsung-wo, who were arrested on Saturday night by the Shanghai Municipal Police in a raid on a house in the French Concession, where Communist literature was found. The accused were brought before the Mixed Court this morning charged with being members of an illegal organisation.

Mr. Ru, for the defence, submitted that his clients should not be handed over to the Chinese authorities unless the Kiangsu High Court made an application. He quoted an article which provides that accused may be handed over only where two courts have concurrent jurisdiction. The despatch sent to the Shanghai & Woosung Gendarmerie Commissioner did not come from a properly constituted law court that had concurrent jurisdiction. If it had come from a proper law court, it would have been sent direct to this Court. Accused should not be handed over to any unlawful authorities.

Special Circumstances in Case.

Judge Yih:—This Court tries all Communist cases excepting those which are of a special nature. In this case, there are special circumstances because the information which led to the arrest of the accused came from the Kiangsu authorities. Some men have been arrested in Kiangsu and they implicated the accused. The Kiangsu authorities, therefore, sent a despatch warrant to the Shanghai and Woosung Gendarmerie Commissioner asking for assistance in arresting them and the Gendarmerie Commissioner, in turn, referred the matter to the Greater Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety. I will not make a ruling this morning because I will have to consult my colleagues. I am not trying this case this morning but I am simply anxious to obtain the views of the Shanghai Municipal Police in the matter.

Mr. Ru:—According to the article quoted, accused should not be handed over unless the Kiangsu High Court makes an application. The article provides that accused may be handed over only where two courts have concurrent jurisdiction. The despatch sent to the Shanghai & Woosung Gendarmerie Commissioner did not come from a properly constituted law court that had concurrent jurisdiction. If it had come from a proper law court, it would have been sent direct to this Court. Accused should not be handed over to any unlawful authorities.

The Kiangsu Application

The Judge said that it was not stated whether the Kiangsu authorities who made the application had concurrent jurisdiction but that would be a point which he would take into his consideration.

Mr. Ru said that all contents of the book store were not necessarily Communists.

Mr. Sung Tsung-wo, for the third accused, said that his client had only been in Shanghai three days and knew nothing about Communism and asked for bail.

The Judge refused bail saying that he would consider the question of bail when the case was fixed for trial. He adjourned the case until tomorrow morning to enable him to consult his colleagues regarding the question of jurisdiction.

混合法庭审判

涉及 alleged 共产党人的重要问题提出

警方突袭的后续

今天上午，在王仲灵、杨印先、吴祖万和徐宗武一案中，提出了一个关于本法庭管辖权的有趣问题。这些人于周六晚被上海公共租界工部局警务处在法租界一处房屋的突袭行动中逮捕，现场发现了共产主义文献。被告今晨被提审至混合法庭，被控为非法组织成员。

辩护律师 Ru 先生提出，除非江苏高等法院提出申请，否则不应将他的当事人移交给中国当局。他引用了一条规定，指出只有在两个法庭拥有共同管辖权的情况下，才可以移交被告。发送给上海及吴淞警备司令部的公文并非来自拥有共同管辖权的正式组建的法律法庭。如果它来自适当的法律法庭，就会直接发送至本法庭。被告不应被移交给任何非法当局。

案件的特殊情况。

易法官（Judge Yih）：— 本法庭审理所有共产党案件，除具有特殊性质的案件外。本案存在特殊情况，因为导致被告被捕的情报来自江苏当局。江苏方面逮捕了一些人，他们牵连了被告。因此，江苏当局向上海及吴淞警备司令部发送了一份协助逮捕令，警备司令部随即将此事转交至上海特别市公安局。我今天上午不作裁决，因为我必须咨询我的同事。我今天上午不审理此案，我只是希望了解上海公共租界工部局警务处对此事的看法。

Ru 先生：— 根据所引用的条款，除非江苏高等法院提出申请，否则不应移交被告。该条款规定，只有在两个法庭拥有共同管辖权的情况下，才可以移交被告。发送给上海及吴淞警备司令部的公文并非来自拥有共同管辖权的正式组建的法律法庭。如果它来自适当的法律法庭，就会直接发送至本法庭。被告不应被移交给任何非法当局。

江苏方面的申请

法官表示，并未说明提出申请的江苏当局是否拥有共同管辖权，但这将是他会考虑的一个要点。

Ru 先生说，书店内的所有物品不一定都是共产主义性质的。

第三位被告的代理人宋宗武（Sung Tsung-wo，音译）先生表示，他的当事人在上海仅待了三天，对共产主义一无所知，并请求保释。

法官拒绝保释，称将在确定庭审日期时考虑保释问题。他将案件延期至明天上午，以便就管辖权问题咨询其同事。
